mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of over 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -1% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by at least 0.3 percentage points in the same month signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month - 0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 2% over the previous month, combined with a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2%, signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month + 2% AND CPIAUCSL < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 1% for six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, supporting risk asset valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 1% for six consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 3%
regime_hint: prolonged monetary accommodation with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.7% for three consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month + 0.7% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.
